simple.meaning: פּוּק (pûwq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to issue , i.e. furnish ; causatively, to secure ; figuratively, to succeed.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 7 times in Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, beginning at Psalms 140:9. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פּוּק (H6329) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פּוּק (pûwq) / H6329 is traced through Psalms 140:9, Psalms 144:13, Proverbs 3:13, Proverbs 8:35 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6329. puq II. מּוּק verb Hiph`il bring out, furnish, promote (Late Hebrew id. ; apparently akin to Aramaic נְפַק go forth , Aph`el bring forth, produce ); — 1 produce, furnish: Imperfect (jussive) לָרָעֵב וְתָפֵק Isa 58:10 with נַפְשְׁךָ (read perhaps לַחְמְךָ see Che Hpt ); Participle אֶלזַֿן מִזַּן מְפִיקִים Psa 144:13 (see זַן ). 2 bring out, elicit, obtain , with accusative; יָפִיק Prov 3:13 , + מִן person, וַיָּפֶק 8:35 ; 18:22 (all || מצא ), 12:2 . 3 אַלתָּֿפֵק זְמָמוֺ Psa 140:9 his device do not promote.
